name: Spacing Effect
description: Information practiced or revisited over spaced intervals is remembered better than the same practice massed together. The best spacing depends on how long the material needs to stick.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to onboarding reinforcement, reminders, progressive disclosure, learning products, habit-building flows, and re-engagement messaging where teams decide when to repeat information or ask users to practice again.
prevalence_note: Central in learning design, edtech, and retention-oriented behavioral product work, but much less universal in general interface-design curricula.

findings.description: Meta-analytic synthesis of 839 assessments across 317 experiments confirms a robust distributed-practice (spacing) advantage over massed practice for verbal recall; the interstudy interval (ISI) that maximizes final-test retention increases as the retention interval increases, meaning optimal spacing is not fixed but scales with how long the material needs to be remembered.
findings.source_title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis.
